the performance of the detectors is affected by challenges such as occlusions, clutter and illumination.
the current state of the art in object detection and pose estimations in RGB-D images is not sufficient for the automation of the robotics tasks.

(1) the current state-of-the-art 6D detectors are able to handle occlusion, clutter and texture in RGB-D images, (2) the performance of the detectors is affected by the size and the pose of the objects, (3) the performance is affected by the quality of the depth data, and (4) the performance is also affected by the type of the object and its appearance.

the community is currently in a good position in terms of automation, but it still requires a lot of effort to achieve autonomy.
the current state of the art for 6D object detection in RGB-D images is not yet at a satisfactory level, since the baselines are unable to handle the challenges in the datasets, which we collected.

, the current state of the art for full 6DOF pose estimation in RGBD images has reached a level that can be used in robotic manipulation.
we provide a thorough multi-modal analysis on 6D object detection, which can help the community in improving “autonomy”, while handling objects.

, the study presents the current position of computer vision in robotic manipulation and discusses the challenges in the datasets, which are collected for evaluating the 6D object detectors, and it suggests the next steps for improving autonomy in robotics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the detectors depends on the challenges involved, the evaluation protocol, and the dataset used, and that there is no “one size fits all” approach to object pose estimation.
the current methods are not yet able to deal with the challenges that are present in the datasets.

, in order to improve the autonomy of the robots, it is necessary to have a thorough multi-modal analysis of the detectors, and the datasets on which they are tested, to understand the limitations of the current approaches and the challenges involved in each dataset.
